mcqs.q: A dental handpiece is a device for:
opts: Holding rotating burs, transmitting power and positioning them intraorally
mcqs.explain: A handpiece holds rotating instruments (burs), transmits power to them and positions them in the mouth.

mcqs.q: According to Sturdevant, HIGH (ultrahigh) speed is defined as:
mcqs.explain: Low/slow = below 12,000 rpm; medium = 12,000–200,000 rpm; high/ultrahigh = above 200,000 rpm.

mcqs.q: Low-speed instruments are indicated for:
opts: Caries excavation in deep lesions and finishing/polishing
mcqs.explain: Low speeds are used for excavating deep caries and for finishing/polishing restorations and teeth.

mcqs.q: An ADVANTAGE of low speed is:
opts: Better tactile sensation (useful in deep caries)
mcqs.explain: Low speed gives better tactile feedback (helpful in deep caries), but it produces more heat, vibration and is slow at cutting.

mcqs.q: A DISADVANTAGE of low speed (requiring coolant) is:
opts: More heat production and vibration, and it is time-consuming
mcqs.explain: Low speed produces more heat (always use water coolant), more vibration, is time-consuming and inefficient for cutting.

mcqs.q: High-speed instruments are mainly indicated for:
opts: Tooth/cavity preparation and removing old restorations
Deep caries excavation with tactile feel
mcqs.explain: High speed is used for tooth/cavity preparation and removing old restorations — faster, with less heat and vibration.

mcqs.q: The three parts of a dental bur are:
mcqs.explain: A bur has a shank (inserted into the handpiece, the longest part), a neck (connector) and a head (working end).

mcqs.q: The working end of a bur is the:
mcqs.explain: The head is the working (cutting) end of the bur.

mcqs.q: Friction-grip burs are used with:
mcqs.explain: By attachment: friction-grip burs fit high-speed handpieces; latch-type burs fit low-speed (contra-angle) handpieces.

mcqs.q: Steel burs perform poorly when:
opts: Used at high speed or cutting enamel (they dull rapidly)
Never — they are best at all tasks
mcqs.explain: Steel burs cut dentin well at low speed but dull rapidly at high speed or when cutting enamel.

mcqs.q: Compared with diamond burs, tungsten-carbide burs:
mcqs.explain: Carbide burs perform better at all speeds and leave a smoother surface than the coarser diamond burs.

mcqs.q: Diamond burs typically leave:
mcqs.explain: Diamond burs grind hard tissue precisely but their coarse grit usually leaves a rough surface.

mcqs.q: The ROUND bur is used for:
opts: Initial entry, extension, retention features and soft-caries removal
mcqs.explain: The spherical round bur (sizes ¼–10) is used for initial entry, extension, retention features and soft-caries removal.

mcqs.q: The INVERTED CONE bur is used for:
opts: Creating undercuts (occlusal convergence) and flattening the pulpal floor
mcqs.explain: The inverted cone bur (33¼–39) makes undercuts (occlusal convergence of walls) and flattens/smooths the pulpal floor.

mcqs.q: The STRAIGHT FISSURE bur (an elongated cylinder) is used for:
mcqs.explain: The straight fissure bur (555–560) is a cylinder used for most of the cavity preparation.

mcqs.q: The TAPERED FISSURE bur (168–172) is advocated for:
opts: Preparations for indirect restorations (cast gold inlays/onlays)
mcqs.explain: The tapered fissure bur (a slightly tapered cone) is used for preparations for indirect restorations such as cast inlays and onlays.

mcqs.q: The long-length pear bur No. 245 is advocated for preparations for:
mcqs.explain: The long pear bur (No. 245) is used for amalgam preparations; the normal pear (No. 330) is used for Class I gold-foil preparations.

mcqs.q: When using low-speed instruments, you should always use:
mcqs.explain: Low speed produces more heat, so a water coolant should always be used.

mcqs.q: The number of blades on a bur is usually:
mcqs.explain: Burs usually have an even number of cutting blades.

mcqs.q: Which speed produces LESS heat and vibration during cutting?
mcqs.explain: High speed produces less heat and vibration and removes tooth structure faster than low speed.

mcqs.q: The part of the bur that is the LONGEST and inserts into the handpiece is the:
mcqs.explain: The shank is usually the longest part of the bur and is inserted into the handpiece.

mcqs.q: A modern improvement in handpieces is:
opts: Smaller head size, lower noise and fibreoptic light
mcqs.explain: Latest handpieces have smaller head sizes, lower noise levels and fibreoptic illumination.

saqs.q: State the three Sturdevant speed ranges.
Give the indications, advantage and disadvantages of low speed.
saqs.a: Indications: caries excavation, finishing/polishing. Advantage: tactile feel. Disadvantages: heat, vibration, slow, poor cutting.

saqs.q: Name the three parts of a bur.

saqs.a: Carbide: better at all speeds, smoother surface. Diamond: powerful/precise on hard tissue but leaves a rougher surface.

saqs.q: Match the bur head shape to its use: round, inverted cone, straight fissure, tapered fissure.
saqs.a: Round: entry/caries; inverted cone: undercuts/pulpal floor; straight fissure: most preps; tapered fissure: inlays/onlays.

saqs.q: Give the advantages of high speed.
saqs.a: Faster removal, less heat, less vibration, time-saving, easier operation, longer instrument life.
